questions.q:
In May 2026 the Union Cabinet approved a proposal to raise the number of judges of the Supreme Court. In this context, consider the following statements:
1. The Constitution as originally enacted provided for a Chief Justice of India and not more than seven other judges.
2. Parliament can raise the number of judges of the Supreme Court by an ordinary law, without amending the Constitution.
3. The sanctioned strength of a High Court is likewise fixed by a law made by Parliament.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Article 124(1) fixed seven judges besides the Chief Justice 'until Parliament by law prescribes a larger number', which is why the strength has been raised through amendments to the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956 and never through Article 368. Statement 3 is wrong: under Article 216 a High Court has a Chief Justice and such other judges as the President may from time to time deem necessary, so its strength is set by executive order.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 16; Articles 124 and 216 are static

questions.q: As a rule used by courts when reading statutes, the 'principle of legality', recalled in the 2026 discussion on constitutionalism and majoritarianism, is the presumption that
o: a penal provision must be read narrowly and in favour of the accused
a later law overrides an earlier law on the same subject
a statute is valid until a court declares it unconstitutional
the legislature did not intend to cut down fundamental rights unless it said so in clear words
questions.e: The principle of legality tells a court to assume that the legislature did not mean to legislate against fundamental rights; general or vague words are therefore not read as taking rights away. It is treated as a working tool of constitutionalism, the idea that power is limited by rules. Treating a statute as valid until struck down is the separate presumption of constitutionality, reading penal provisions narrowly is the rule of strict construction, and a later law prevailing over an earlier one is the doctrine of implied repeal.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs relating to Public Interest Litigation (PIL) in India:
Case : Subject or holding
1. Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar : Condition of undertrial prisoners
2. People's Union for Democratic Rights v. Union of India : Labour-law violations in construction for the Asian Games
3. Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan : Sexual harassment of women at the workplace
4. State of Jharkhand v. Shiv Shankar Sharma : The petitioner's bona fides need be examined only at the final hearing
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Hussainara Khatoon (1979) is regarded as the first PIL and led to the release of undertrials; the PUDR case (1982) took up the exploitation of workers on Asiad projects; Vishaka (1997) produced guidelines that became the basis of the 2013 law on workplace harassment. Pair 4 is wrong: in the Shiv Shankar Sharma case (2022) the Court said the petitioner's credentials and motive must be tested at the threshold, before the petition is entertained.

questions.q: A petition seeking the disqualification of members of the Rajya Sabha for defection, such as the one filed in 2026 after several members of one party joined another, is decided in the first instance by the
o: President, acting on the opinion of the Election Commission of India
Committee of Privileges of the Rajya Sabha
Supreme Court in its original jurisdiction
questions.e: Under Paragraph 6 of the Tenth Schedule the question of disqualification on the ground of defection is decided by the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha or the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, as the case may be. The President acting on the Election Commission's opinion decides the other disqualifications, such as office of profit, under Article 103, which is the usual confusion. A committee may assist with inquiry but does not decide, and courts step in only by way of judicial review after the presiding officer's decision.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 15; Article 103 is static

questions.q:
Reliance on ordinances was cited in 2026 as a challenge to constitutionalism. In this context, consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Supreme Court has held that repeated re-promulgation of ordinances without placing them before the legislature is a fraud on the Constitution.
Statement-II: An ordinance promulgated by a Governor remains in force for one year from the date of promulgation unless it is withdrawn earlier.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: in D.C. Wadhwa v. State of Bihar (1987), which dealt with Bihar ordinances kept alive for years by re-promulgation, the Court called the practice a fraud on the Constitution, and a larger bench repeated this in Krishna Kumar Singh (2017). Statement-II is incorrect. Under Article 213 an ordinance must be laid before the legislature and ceases to operate six weeks after the legislature reassembles, unless it is disapproved or withdrawn earlier.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 6-7; Article 213 and D.C. Wadhwa (1987) are static

questions.q:
With reference to the Panchayat Advancement Index (PAI) 2.0, released in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It is brought out by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj.
2. It scores Gram Panchayats on nine themes drawn from the Localisation of Sustainable Development Goals.
3. It ranks States on how far they have devolved funds, functions and functionaries to Panchayats.
4. In this round, data submitted by a Gram Panchayat had to be validated by the Gram Sabha.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The Index measures the progress of individual Gram Panchayats on nine themes into which the 17 Sustainable Development Goals are grouped, and PAI 2.0 made Gram Sabha validation compulsory. Statement 3 describes the separate Devolution Index, which compares States on the transfer of funds, functions and functionaries. PAI grades each Panchayat from Achiever down to Beginner; no Panchayat reached the Achiever grade in this round.

questions.q: In a State Assembly, a 'composite floor test' is best described as
o: a confidence motion and a no-confidence motion taken up together in one sitting
a vote in which members of both Houses of a bicameral State legislature take part
a single vote that tests rival claims at once, held when more than one person stakes a claim to form the government
a floor test in which voice vote, electronic vote and division are all used in turn
questions.e: An ordinary floor test asks whether the Chief Minister in office has the confidence of the Assembly. A composite floor test is used when two or more claimants each say they command a majority; the House votes once and the claims are settled together, with the count taken of members present and voting. The Legislative Council has no role in any trust vote because the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible only to the Assembly. The other descriptions are invented.

questions.q:
With reference to the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, which was under challenge before the Supreme Court in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The Selection Committee may recommend a person who is not on the panel of names prepared by the Search Committee.
2. Salaries and service conditions of Election Commissioners continue to be governed by the Election Commission Act of 1991.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the Act lets the Selection Committee, made up of the Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister and the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, consider any other person besides the shortlisted names, which is one reason petitioners say the search stage can be bypassed. Statement 2 is wrong. The 2023 Act repealed the Election Commission (Conditions of Service of Election Commissioners and Transaction of Business) Act, 1991 and now covers appointment, service conditions and term together.

questions.q:
With reference to the anti-defection law in the Tenth Schedule, invoked in 2026 in a plea against Rajya Sabha members who left their party, consider the following statements:
1. A member who votes or abstains contrary to the party whip, without prior permission and without condonation by the party within fifteen days, is liable to disqualification.
2. The merger exception applies where the member's original political party merges with another and at least two-thirds of the legislature party agree to the merger.
3. A breakaway group of one-third of the legislature party continues to be protected from disqualification.
4. A person elected as Speaker or Chairman may give up party membership on taking office without incurring disqualification on that account.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Paragraph 2 makes defying the whip a ground, subject to prior permission or condonation within fifteen days. Paragraph 4 protects a merger of the original political party backed by two-thirds of its legislature party, which is why the 2026 plea argues that legislators cannot merge on their own. Paragraph 5 lets a presiding officer step out of his party. Statement 3 is wrong: the one-third 'split' protection was deleted in 2003 by the 91st Amendment, so only a merger now saves a defector.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 15; Paragraphs 2, 4 and 5 of the Tenth Schedule are static

questions.q: The Supreme Court's FASTER system, mentioned along with prison reforms in 2026, is meant to
o: let prisoners appear before trial courts by video link from inside jails
maintain a national database of prisoners that States can update in real time
list bail applications of undertrial prisoners automatically before a bench within a fixed time
send certified copies of orders such as bail and stay orders electronically to courts and jail authorities through a secure channel
questions.e: FASTER stands for Fast and Secured Transmission of Electronic Records. It was created after cases in which prisoners stayed in jail for days because the paper copy of a bail order had not reached the prison; authenticated e-copies now go directly to the authorities concerned. The national prisoner database is the E-Prisons project developed by the National Informatics Centre. Video appearance and automatic listing are separate measures, the first recommended by the Justice Amitava Roy Committee.

questions.q:
The office of Chief Minister came into focus after the West Bengal Assembly election of 2026. In this context, consider the following statements:
1. The Constitution does not fix a term of office for the Chief Minister.
2. Article 167 places a duty on the Chief Minister to communicate to the Governor the decisions of the Council of Ministers on administration and proposals for legislation.
3. A person who is not a member of the State legislature may be appointed Chief Minister but must get elected to it within six months.
4. Article 164 fixes the Chief Minister's tenure at five years, to run with the life of the Assembly.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor and has no fixed tenure; in practice he continues while he enjoys the confidence of the Assembly. Article 167 makes him the channel of communication between the Council of Ministers and the Governor, and Article 164(4) lets a non-member be appointed but requires him to win a seat within six months. Statement 4 is wrong: the five-year period in Article 172 belongs to the Assembly, not to the Chief Minister, which is why the West Bengal debate turned on convention and the floor test.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 3-5; Article 164(4) is static

questions.q:
With reference to the directions in State of Uttarakhand v. Balwant Singh Chaufal (2010) on Public Interest Litigation, which of the following are correct?
1. Each High Court should frame rules to encourage genuine petitions and discourage those filed with oblique motives.
2. A petition may be entertained only when it is filed by a registered organisation.
3. Courts should verify, prima facie, the credentials of the petitioner and the correctness of the contents.
4. Petitions involving larger public interest, gravity and urgency should get priority.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Statements 1, 3 and 4 reflect the Chaufal directions, which were issued to keep the PIL route open for real grievances while filtering out private, political or publicity-driven petitions. The Court asked for a threshold check of the petitioner and the facts, for High Court rules, and for priority to matters of wider public importance. Statement 2 is wrong: the whole idea of PIL is relaxed locus standi, so any public-spirited person may petition, and no registration requirement was laid down.

questions.q:
In the context of the anti-defection law, consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Ninety-first Constitutional Amendment omitted the provision that protected a 'split' by one-third of the members of a legislature party.
Statement-II: The Ninety-first Constitutional Amendment limited the size of the Council of Ministers to fifteen per cent of the strength of the lower House.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct, but the second does not explain the first. The 2003 amendment did two separate things. It deleted Paragraph 3 of the Tenth Schedule, so that a breakaway group of one-third can no longer escape disqualification and only a merger backed by two-thirds is protected. It also added a ceiling on ministries in Articles 75 and 164, with a floor of twelve ministers for smaller States, to curb the use of ministerial posts as rewards for defectors.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 15; the ceiling on ministries is static

questions.q: Paragraph 16A of the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968 was cited in 2026 in the debate on the Model Code of Conduct. It empowers the Election Commission of India to
o: cancel the registration of a political party that does not contest elections for six years
disqualify a candidate who uses official machinery for campaigning
suspend or withdraw the recognition of a recognised political party that fails to observe the Model Code or the Commission's lawful directions
decide which of two rival factions of a recognised party is entitled to the reserved symbol
questions.e: Paragraph 16A is the Commission's strongest tool behind a Code that has no statute of its own: a party that ignores the Code or lawful directions can have its recognition suspended or withdrawn after a hearing. Deciding between rival factions is done under Paragraph 15 of the same Order. The Commission has no express power to deregister a party for inactivity, and a candidate can be disqualified for corrupt practice only through an election petition and the process that follows it.

questions.q:
Regarding election petitions, relevant after the Assembly elections of 2026, consider the following statements:
1. An election petition calling in question an election to a State Assembly is tried by the High Court.
2. It must be presented within forty-five days of the date of poll in the constituency.
3. It may be presented by any candidate at the election or by any elector of the constituency.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Article 329 allows an election to be questioned only by an election petition, tried since 1966 by the High Court, and Section 81 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 lets any candidate or any elector present it. Statement 2 is wrong: the forty-five days run from the date of election of the returned candidate, that is, the declaration of the result, and not from polling day. Section 100 lists the grounds, such as corrupt practices, on which the High Court can declare an election void.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 3-5; Sections 80A, 81 and 100 of the RPA 1951 are static

questions.q:
The National Testing Agency (NTA) was in the news in May 2026 over the NEET-UG examination. Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The NTA was designed on the model of the Educational Testing Service of the United States.
Statement-II: The NTA functions under the Department of Higher Education of the Ministry of Education.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct, yet one does not explain the other. The agency was approved in 2017 and began work in 2018 as a specialised testing body, borrowing the idea of a dedicated assessment organisation from the Educational Testing Service. Its administrative parent is the Department of Higher Education, even though the largest test it runs, NEET-UG, is for medical courses overseen by the Health Ministry. That split is one reason a shift of NEET to computer-based mode needs a decision by both ministries.

questions.q:
With reference to Finance Commissions, in the news in 2026 over the award of the Sixteenth Finance Commission, consider the following statements:
1. The Constitution itself lays down the qualifications required of the members of the Commission.
2. The Chairman is to be selected from among persons who have had experience in public affairs.
3. The law requires that one member be, or be qualified to be appointed as, a Judge of the Supreme Court.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Article 280 leaves qualifications to Parliament, which enacted the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951. That Act asks for a Chairman with experience in public affairs and four members drawn from four fields: a person who is or is qualified to be a High Court judge, a person with special knowledge of government finance and accounts, one with wide experience in financial matters and administration, and one with special knowledge of economics. There is no requirement of a Supreme Court judge.

questions.q:
With reference to the Model Code of Conduct, consider the following statements:
1. A code of this kind was first tried in Kerala during the Assembly election of 1960.
2. The part dealing with the 'party in power' was added later, in 1979.
3. It has no statutory backing and rests on the Election Commission's authority under Article 324.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. The Code began as a set of norms agreed for the 1960 Kerala election, was taken up by the Election Commission in the late 1960s and was enlarged in 1979 with a section restraining the ruling party from using official visits, government machinery and public media for campaigning. It remains a voluntary code without a statute; its force comes from Article 324, from overlap with offences in election and penal law, and from the Commission's power over party recognition.

questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the Citizenship (Amendment) Rules, 2026 are correct?
1. They were notified by the Ministry of Home Affairs.
2. Overseas Citizen of India status can now be issued in electronic form.
3. An applicant under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 must declare on affidavit whether he holds a valid or expired passport of Pakistan, Afghanistan or Bangladesh.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: All three are correct. Citizenship is a Union subject administered by the Home Ministry, which notified the Rules. They move Overseas Citizen of India services fully online and allow an e-OCI alongside the physical card, with mandatory surrender of the card on renunciation or cancellation. Applicants under the 2019 Act must disclose any passport of the three named countries. The Rules also bar a minor who holds an Indian passport from holding another country's passport at any time.

questions.q:
The International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) was cited in the 2026 debate on academic freedom. With reference to it, consider the following statements:
1. Its implementation is monitored by the Human Rights Committee, a body of independent experts.
2. The Second Optional Protocol to the Covenant aims at the abolition of the death penalty.
3. India has accepted the individual complaints procedure under the First Optional Protocol.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Human Rights Committee, which should not be confused with the inter-governmental Human Rights Council, reviews State reports under the Covenant, and the Second Optional Protocol commits parties to abolish capital punishment. Statement 3 is wrong: India acceded to the Covenant in 1979 but has not joined the First Optional Protocol, so a person in India cannot take an individual complaint to the Committee after exhausting remedies at home.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 26-28; the treaty bodies are static

questions.q: Which one of the following bodies recommended that Election Commissioners be chosen by a collegium that would include the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
o: The Law Commission of India in its 255th Report
The Supreme Court in the Anoop Baranwal case
questions.e: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission proposed a wider political collegium: the Prime Minister, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, the Law Minister and the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. The Tarkunde Committee and the Law Commission's 255th Report both suggested a three-member panel of the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition and the Chief Justice of India, and the Anoop Baranwal judgment put that three-member panel in place as an interim arrangement until Parliament legislated.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the report 'Prison Statistics India 2024':
1. The occupancy rate of prisons fell compared with the previous year but stayed above 100 per cent.
2. The report is published by the Bureau of Police Research and Development.
3. 'Prisons' is a subject in the State List of the Seventh Schedule.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Occupancy eased from about 121 per cent to about 113 per cent as capacity grew and the number of inmates fell, which still means overcrowding. Prisons and persons detained in them fall under Entry 4 of the State List, which is why the Centre works through model manuals and model laws. Statement 2 is wrong: the report comes from the National Crime Records Bureau, which also publishes 'Crime in India' and 'Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India'.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 15-16; Entry 4 of the State List is static

questions.q:
On the role of the Governor, consider the following statements:
Statement-I: In A.G. Perarivalan v. State (2022) the Supreme Court described the Governor as a shorthand expression for the State Government.
Statement-II: The Governor exercises the executive power of the State on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers, except where the Constitution requires him to act in his discretion.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct and the second explains the first. Article 154 vests executive power in the Governor, but Article 163 requires that he act on ministerial advice save in matters of discretion. Because decisions taken in his name are in substance those of the elected government, the Court in the Perarivalan case treated the word 'Governor' as standing for the State Government. The same reasoning limits a literal reading of the phrase 'pleasure of the Governor' in Article 164.

questions.q:
Tripura in 2026 completed all priority areas of Phase-II of the National Compliance Reduction and Deregulation Initiative. With reference to this initiative, consider the following statements:
1. The Task Force that steers the initiative is chaired by the Chief Executive Officer of NITI Aayog.
2. Its priority areas lie chiefly in Union List subjects such as banking and telecommunications.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither statement is correct. The Task Force on Compliance Reduction and Deregulation was set up in 2025 under the Cabinet Secretary. Its 23 priority areas, grouped in five broad sectors, concern matters that States regulate: land, building and construction, utilities and permissions, labour and similar fields. The exercise therefore works by guiding States to amend their own laws and procedures, and Phase-II, begun in January 2026, widened it to areas such as environment, education and health.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II, with reference to corrupt practices under Section 123 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, discussed in 2026 in connection with a broadcast by the Prime Minister:
List-I
A. Section 123(1)
B. Section 123(2)
C. Section 123(3)
D. Section 123(7)
List-II
1. Appeal to vote on the ground of religion, race, caste, community or language
2. Obtaining the assistance of persons in government service to further a candidate's prospects
3. Bribery
4. Undue influence
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Section 123 lists corrupt practices that can void an election. Clause (1) is bribery and clause (2) undue influence. Clause (3) concerns the ground of the appeal: religion, race, caste, community or language. Clause (7) concerns who was pressed into service: gazetted officers, police, members of the armed forces and other government servants. The 2026 writ petition relied on clause (7), arguing that public broadcasters and official staff were used, because an appeal built on gender and party does not fit clause (3).

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of a system in the justice sector and a feature of it:
System : Feature
1. FASTER : Secure electronic transmission of court orders
2. E-Prisons : Developed by the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing
3. e-Courts Mission Mode Project : Taken up under the National e-Governance Plan
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct. FASTER carries authenticated copies of Supreme Court orders to the authorities who must act on them. The e-Courts project, begun in 2007 under the National e-Governance Plan, is run by the Department of Justice with the e-Committee of the Supreme Court; under it Sikkim was declared the first paperless State judiciary in 2026. Pair 2 is wrong because the E-Prisons prisoner-information system was built by the National Informatics Centre.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 17; Vision IAS pp. 15-16

questions.q: Which one of the following best describes the recommendation of the K. Radhakrishnan Committee for a 'computer-assisted secure pen-and-paper test'?
o: Printed question papers travel in GPS-tracked vehicles and are opened under CCTV
Answer sheets are scanned at the centre and evaluated by software on the same day
Candidates answer on tablets that are supplied and collected by the testing agency
Question papers are sent to the centre in encrypted digital form and printed there shortly before the examination
questions.e: The Committee, set up by the Education Ministry after the 2024 NEET-UG controversy and headed by a former ISRO chief, wanted to remove the weakest link, which is the physical journey of printed papers. In its hybrid model the paper stays encrypted until it reaches the centre and is printed locally just before the test, while a phased move to full computer-based testing continues. GPS-tracked transport and CCTV were the existing safeguards that failed in 2026.

questions.q:
Which of the following statements about a floor test in a State Legislative Assembly are correct?
1. The majority is counted of the members present and voting.
2. When the Assembly is in session, it is for the Speaker to hold the test.
3. In the event of a tie, the presiding officer exercises a casting vote.
4. Members who abstain are counted as having voted against the motion.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. A confidence motion is carried by a majority of those present and voting, so members who stay away or abstain simply lower the number needed; they are not counted on either side, which makes statement 4 wrong. The Speaker conducts the vote when the House is sitting, and the Governor can summon the House and ask for a test when it is not. Under Article 189 the presiding officer votes only to break a tie.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 3-5; Article 189 is static

questions.q:
With reference to laws and registers on population data, mentioned in connection with the High-Level Committee on Demographic Changes, consider the following pairs:
Register or system : Legal basis
1. National Population Register : Census Act, 1948
2. Civil Registration System : Citizenship Act, 1955
3. Sample Registration System : Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: None of the pairs is correct; the legal bases are jumbled. The National Population Register is prepared under the Citizenship Act, 1955 and the 2003 Rules made under it. The Civil Registration System, the continuous and compulsory recording of births and deaths, rests on the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969. The Sample Registration System is a large demographic survey of the Registrar General's office and has no statute of its own. The Census is the exercise held under the Census Act, 1948.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 28-30; the statutes are static

questions.q:
The Supreme Court observed in 2026 that majoritarianism cannot override constitutionalism. Consider the following pairs of a case and what it decided:
1. I.R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu : Laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 are open to challenge on the basic structure test
2. Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India : Consensual same-sex relations between adults were decriminalised
3. K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India : Privacy is a fundamental right under Article 21
4. Rameshwar Prasad v. Union of India : Dissolution of the Bihar Assembly on the Governor's report was upheld
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct, and each shows a court limiting what a majority may do: Coelho ended the blanket immunity of the Ninth Schedule, Navtej Johar read down Section 377 despite social prejudice, and Puttaswamy placed privacy within Article 21. Pair 4 is wrong. In Rameshwar Prasad (2006) the Court held the 2005 dissolution of the Bihar Assembly unconstitutional, saying that constitutionalism abhors absolutism and that subjective satisfaction must yield to constitutional standards.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 6-7; the holdings are static

questions.q:
On the tenure of a Chief Minister, consider the following statements:
Statement-I: A Governor cannot dismiss a Chief Minister who commands a majority in the Assembly merely by withdrawing his 'pleasure'.
Statement-II: B.R. Ambedkar explained in the Constituent Assembly that a ministry holds office only so long as it enjoys the confidence of the majority.
Statement-III: Article 164 makes the Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both of them explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct, but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: Statements II and III are both correct and both explain Statement-I. Read literally, 'pleasure of the Governor' in Article 164 suggests a free power of dismissal. The framers declined to spell out the confidence requirement because, as Ambedkar said, it is implicit in every parliamentary system, and the same Article ties the ministry to the Assembly through collective responsibility. The pleasure therefore follows the confidence of the House, and a Governor may act only when that confidence is lost.

questions.q: In debates on the misuse of Public Interest Litigation, an 'ambush PIL' refers to a petition that is
o: filed without notice to the government so as to obtain an ex parte stay
filed by a business rival to stall a competitor's project in the name of the environment
sent as a letter to a judge and treated as a writ petition
filed in a deliberately weak form so that it is dismissed and blocks a genuine challenge on the same issue
questions.e: An ambush PIL is a set-up: the petition is drafted poorly on purpose, invites dismissal, and the dismissal is then used to shut out serious litigants who raise the same question later. It is one of the abuses that led the Supreme Court to criticise the misuse of PILs in 2026. A petition by a rival is private-interest litigation dressed as public interest. A letter treated as a writ petition is the court's epistolary jurisdiction, which is a legitimate practice.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 226 a High Court may issue writs not only for the enforcement of fundamental rights but also for any other purpose.
2. The rights in Articles 29 and 30 are available to religious minorities but not to linguistic minorities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Article 226 is wider than Article 32: a High Court can issue writs for fundamental rights and 'for any other purpose', which is how courts police the legality of executive action; with Article 13 this judicial review is one of the checks that keep power within limits, as the 2026 observation on constitutionalism stressed. Statement 2 is wrong. Article 30 expressly protects minorities 'whether based on religion or language' in setting up and running educational institutions, and Article 29 protects any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 6-7; Articles 29, 30 and 226 are static

questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order, earliest first:
1. Supreme Court's judgment in the Anoop Baranwal case
2. Report of the Tarkunde Committee
3. Report of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission on ethics in governance
4. 255th Report of the Law Commission of India
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Tarkunde Committee reported in 1975, the Second Administrative Reforms Commission in 2007, the Law Commission in 2015 and the Supreme Court decided the Anoop Baranwal case in March 2023. All four asked for a selection body wider than the executive for Election Commissioners. Parliament then passed the 2023 Act, which kept the Prime Minister and the Leader of Opposition but put a Union Cabinet Minister in the place the Court had given to the Chief Justice of India.

questions.q:
NITI Aayog released a framework for million-plus cities in 2026. With reference to it and to urban local government, consider the following statements:
1. The Twelfth Schedule lists twenty-nine functions for municipalities.
2. The framework suggests market borrowing by cities, for example through municipal bonds.
3. The framework wants water, sanitation and transport to stay with State-level parastatal bodies outside the city government's oversight.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. The Twelfth Schedule, added by the 74th Amendment, lists eighteen functions; twenty-nine is the number of subjects in the Eleventh Schedule for Panchayats. The report says city governments fully control only a few of the eighteen, and it asks for directly elected Mayors with a fixed tenure, own-source revenue, timely State Finance Commission transfers and municipal bonds. It wants services integrated under the city government and parastatals brought under city oversight, the reverse of statement 3.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Finance Commission is not correct?
o: Its suggestions for augmenting a State's Consolidated Fund to supplement the resources of Panchayats rest on the recommendations of that State's Finance Commission.
It is constituted by the President every fifth year or at such earlier time as he considers necessary.
Its Chairman and members are appointed by the President on the recommendation of the Inter-State Council.
It recommends the principles that should govern grants-in-aid of the revenues of the States out of the Consolidated Fund of India.
questions.e: The statement about the Inter-State Council is the wrong one: Article 280 simply provides for appointment by the President, and the 1951 Act on the subject deals only with qualifications and disqualifications. The other three statements follow the text of Article 280, including the duty added by the 73rd and 74th Amendments to suggest measures for local bodies on the basis of State Finance Commission reports. States' unease with the Sixteenth Commission's award in 2026 concerned the formula and not the manner of appointment.

questions.q:
With reference to Public Interest Litigation, consider the following statements:
1. The idea of public interest litigation first took shape in the United Kingdom in the 1980s.
2. 'Representative social action' concerns diffuse rights of the public at large, while 'citizen social action' seeks redress for a determinate disadvantaged class.
3. In the Balwant Singh Chaufal case the Supreme Court advised against imposing costs on PIL petitioners so that access to courts is not discouraged.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None of the statements is correct. Public interest litigation grew out of the United States in the 1960s and was adapted in India from the late 1970s. The two categories are reversed: representative social action is brought for an identifiable disadvantaged group, such as bonded labourers, whereas citizen social action asserts collective rights of the wider public, such as a clean environment. The Chaufal directions of 2010 in fact called for exemplary costs on busybodies who file frivolous petitions.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The National Institution for Transforming India's 2026 report on million-plus cities recommended directly elected Mayors with a fixed tenure.
Statement-II: The Constitution, after the 74th Amendment, requires that the Mayor of every Municipal Corporation be directly elected by voters for a term of five years.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: the report finds that Mayors are not the real heads of city governments and asks for directly elected Mayors with fixed tenure and an empowered Mayor-in-Council. Statement-II is incorrect. Article 243R leaves the manner of election of the chairperson of a municipality to the State legislature, which is why some States elect Mayors directly, others through councillors, and terms range from one year to five. The recommendation therefore calls for States to amend their municipal laws.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 13-14; Article 243R is static

questions.q:
With reference to the regulation of online gaming, consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Under the Seventh Schedule, the States have no legislative competence over betting and gambling.
Statement-II: Parliament enacted a law in 2025 that prohibits online money games and provides for promotion of e-sports and online social games.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect: 'betting and gambling' is Entry 34 of the State List, and States have long had their own gaming laws. Statement-II is correct. The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 bans games played with money stakes and supports e-sports and social games, and the Rules that took effect on 1 May 2026 put it into operation. The overlap between the State entry and a central law for an online, cross-border activity is the federal question the framework raises.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 5-8; Entry 34 of the State List is static

questions.q:
With reference to corrupt practices under election law, consider the following statements:
1. In Abhiram Singh v. C.D. Commachen (2017) the Supreme Court held that the word 'his' in Section 123(3) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 refers only to the religion of the candidate.
2. A corrupt practice under Section 123 can be made a ground for declaring an election void in an election petition.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 2 is correct: under Section 100 a High Court can set aside an election if a corrupt practice by the returned candidate or with his consent is proved. Statement 1 is wrong. A seven-judge bench, by four to three, read 'his' widely to cover the religion, race, caste, community or language of the candidate, his agent, the rival and also the voter. The provision still deals only with those five grounds, so an appeal framed around gender or party falls outside it.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) scheme:
1. An OCI cardholder is not required to report to the police however long he stays in India.
2. A person who is or has been a citizen of Pakistan or Bangladesh is not eligible.
3. OCI cardholders have parity with non-resident Indians in all economic matters, including purchase of agricultural land.
4. Under the Citizenship (Amendment) Rules, 2026 a revision against an order on OCI is heard by an authority one rank above the authority that passed the order.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. A cardholder gets a lifelong multiple-entry visa and need not report to the police; those who are or were citizens of Pakistan, Bangladesh or another notified country are ineligible; and under the 2026 Rules a revision lies to an authority one rank above the deciding authority. Statement 3 is wrong: parity with non-resident Indians stops short of acquiring agricultural or plantation property, and the card carries no political rights. OCI is a privilege that can be cancelled, not dual citizenship.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Model Code of Conduct is not correct?
o: It comes into operation when the Election Commission announces the election schedule.
It applies to organisations, corporations and commissions funded by the government as well as to parties and candidates.
It restrains the party in power from using publicly funded media for partisan coverage.
A breach of any of its provisions is by itself an offence triable under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
questions.e: The statement that a breach is by itself a triable offence is the incorrect one. The Code is a set of agreed norms without a statute; a breach attracts censure, advisories or action against party recognition, and it becomes punishable only where the same act is also an offence or corrupt practice under election or penal law. The other statements are right: the Punjab and Haryana High Court in Harbans Singh Jalal (1997) accepted enforcement from the date of announcement, the Code reaches government-funded bodies, and its part on the party in power deals with misuse of official media.

questions.q:
Under the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Rules, 2026, which came into force on 1 May 2026, the Authority looks at certain factors to decide whether a game is an 'online money game'. Consider the following:
1. Whether the outcome depends mainly on skill and not on chance
2. Whether fees or stakes are paid to take part
3. Whether players expect monetary winnings
4. Whether in-game assets can be turned into money outside the game
How many of the above are factors to be considered?
questions.e: Items 2, 3 and 4 are listed factors, together with the revenue model of the game. Item 1 is not: the 2025 Act prohibits online money games whether they rest on skill, chance or both, so the old 'game of skill' defence no longer decides the matter. A determination can start on the Authority's own motion, on a provider's application or on a Central notification, and the order is to be made within ninety days.

questions.q:
Which of the following functions are listed in the Twelfth Schedule of the Constitution?
1. Fire services
2. Urban forestry and protection of the environment
3. Vital statistics including registration of births and deaths
4. Public order
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The first three are among the eighteen functions that Article 243W allows a State to assign to municipalities, along with urban planning, water supply, public health and sanitation, slum improvement and roads and bridges. Public order is not in the Schedule; with police it belongs to the State List and stays with the State government. NITI Aayog's 2026 report noted that even the listed functions have been devolved only in part, with city governments in full control of very few of them.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 13-14; the Twelfth Schedule is static

questions.q: The Fast Track Immigration Programme, for which applicants for Overseas Citizen of India status may now give consent to share biometrics, is meant to
o: replace the passport with a digital travel credential for travel within South Asia
let pre-verified Indian nationals and OCI cardholders clear immigration quickly through automated gates
speed up the grant of citizenship to long-term residents of Indian origin
give visa on arrival to nationals of countries with which India has reciprocal arrangements
questions.e: The programme is a trusted-traveller facility: a person enrols once with biometrics and can then pass through e-gates at notified airports without the usual counter check. The 2026 citizenship rules allow an applicant for the card to agree, at the time of applying, to share biometrics for automatic enrolment. It has nothing to do with visas on arrival or with the grant of citizenship, and a passport is still needed for travel.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 14-15; the Fast Track Immigration Programme is static

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of a report or index and the body that brings it out:
1. Democracy Report : Freedom House
2. Free to Think : Scholars at Risk
3. Freedom in the World : V-Dem Institute
4. Academic Freedom Index : UNESCO
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 2 is correct. 'Free to Think' is the yearly record of attacks on higher education by the network Scholars at Risk. The Democracy Report, which again placed India among 'electoral autocracies' in 2026, comes from the V-Dem Institute in Sweden, and 'Freedom in the World' is the Freedom House survey; the two are swapped here. The Academic Freedom Index is produced with V-Dem data by researchers of a German university and V-Dem, not by UNESCO.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 26-28; Freedom House and the Academic Freedom Index are static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Election Commission of India enforces the Model Code of Conduct although no statute enacts the Code.
Statement-II: In Mohinder Singh Gill v. Chief Election Commissioner (1978) the Supreme Court described Article 324 as a reservoir of power for areas left unoccupied by legislation.
Statement-III: The Representation of the People Act, 1951 expressly empowers the Commission to punish breaches of the Model Code.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both of them explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct, but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: Statement-II is correct and explains Statement-I: where Parliament has made no law, the Commission can draw on its plenary power of superintendence, direction and control under Article 324, and it is on this footing that the Code is enforced. Statement-III is incorrect. The 1951 Act deals with electoral offences and corrupt practices and does not mention the Code; proposals to give the Code statutory force have not been acted upon.

questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the High-Level Committee on Demographic Changes, constituted in 2026, are correct?
1. It was set up by a resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs.
2. It is chaired by a retired judge of the Supreme Court.
3. The Census Commissioner of India is a member.
4. It is a statutory commission created under the Citizenship Act, 1955.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Committee was created by an executive resolution, is headed by a former Supreme Court judge and includes the Census Commissioner, a Joint Secretary of the Home Ministry as member-secretary and outside experts. It has a year to report, with a limited extension. Statement 4 is wrong: it has no statutory basis, and one of its tasks is to say whether a dedicated law on demographic change is needed.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the National Sports Board and the National Sports Tribunal, for which Rules were notified in 2026, is not correct?
o: The Chairperson and Members of the Board are appointed by the Central Government on the recommendation of a Search-cum-Selection Committee.
Orders of the Tribunal can be enforced in the same way as decrees of a civil court.
The accounts of the Board are audited by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
Online money games may be registered as e-sports under the National Sports Governance Act, 2025.
questions.e: The statement on online money games is the incorrect one: the online gaming rules of 2026 state that a game played with money stakes cannot be recognised or registered as an e-sport under the sports governance law. The remaining statements describe the new bodies correctly. The Board keeps records of national sports bodies and frames model governance guidelines, while the Tribunal is meant to take sports disputes out of the ordinary courts and can pass interim orders after a hearing.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 12-13; Shankar IAS pp. 5-8

questions.q: In the classification used by the V-Dem Institute, whose 2026 report again placed India in this category, an 'electoral autocracy' is a regime in which
o: multiparty elections are held, but they fall short of democratic standards because of deficits in freedoms such as expression and association and in the fairness of the process
no multiparty elections are held for the chief executive or the legislature
elections are free and fair but the judiciary and legislature fail to restrain the executive
power alternates between two parties that keep others out through electoral law
questions.e: V-Dem sorts regimes into closed autocracy, electoral autocracy, electoral democracy and liberal democracy. A closed autocracy has no multiparty elections. An electoral autocracy holds them, but the conditions that make elections meaningful, such as free expression, free association and a clean process, are found wanting. Free and fair elections with weak checks on the executive would be an electoral democracy, one step below a liberal democracy. Such rankings are contested by governments, including India's.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 26-28; the four regime types are static

questions.q:
With reference to the High-Level Committee on examination reforms set up after the NEET-UG controversy of 2024, consider the following statements:
1. It favoured a phased shift of large pen-and-paper tests to computer-based testing, with safeguards for rural and regional-language candidates.
2. It was constituted by the Supreme Court and reports to it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. The panel headed by K. Radhakrishnan wanted a gradual move to computer-based tests on the pattern of JEE Main, more secure centres including upgraded Kendriya and Navodaya Vidyalayas, and digital delivery of encrypted papers in the interim. Statement 2 is wrong: the Education Ministry set up the Committee, although the Supreme Court had also examined the 2024 leak. The 2026 leak revived the charge that the recommendations were not carried out in full.

questions.q:
The principle of non-refoulement was raised in 2026 in connection with proposals on the repatriation of illegal foreigners. Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: India is not bound, as a matter of treaty obligation, by the non-refoulement provision of the Refugee Convention.
Statement-II: India has acceded neither to the Convention relating to the Status of Refugees, 1951 nor to its 1967 Protocol.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct and the second explains the first. Non-refoulement, in Article 33 of the 1951 Convention, forbids returning a person to a place where his life or freedom is threatened. India is outside the Convention and the Protocol and treats foreigners under the general law on foreigners and citizenship. Courts have nonetheless tested deportations against Article 21, which protects non-citizens too, and that is why judicial scrutiny is listed among the concerns about the new Committee's mandate.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 28-30; the Refugee Convention is static

questions.q:
With reference to committees and court decisions on prison reform, consider the following pairs:
Committee or case : Associated with
1. Justice A.N. Mulla Committee : An all-India service for prisons and correctional administration
2. Justice Amitava Roy Committee : Special fast-track courts and use of video conferencing
3. Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer Committee : Women prisoners
4. Suhas Chakma v. Union of India : Wider use of open prisons
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All four pairs are correct. The Mulla Committee of the early 1980s proposed an Indian Prisons and Correctional Service and steps to cut the number of undertrials. The Krishna Iyer Committee of 1987 dealt with women prisoners. The Amitava Roy Committee, appointed by the Supreme Court, suggested fast-track courts and video links to reduce overcrowding. In the Suhas Chakma case (2024) the Court pressed for open prisons, which the 2024 prison statistics make relevant since occupancy is still above capacity.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 15-16; the Krishna Iyer Committee is static

questions.q:
With reference to the constitutional setting of the debate on demographic change and illegal migration, consider the following statements:
1. 'Police' and 'public order' are subjects in the State List.
2. The protection of Article 21 extends to persons who are not citizens of India.
3. The Sixth Schedule applies to tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. Because police and public order are State subjects, a centrally designed mechanism to identify, detain and repatriate illegal foreigners needs the cooperation of State governments, which is the federal friction noted in 2026. Article 21 speaks of 'person' and not 'citizen', so any such mechanism must follow a fair procedure. The Sixth Schedule covers autonomous districts in the four named north-eastern States, which are among the tribal belts the Home Ministry flagged.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 28-30; the constitutional provisions are static

questions.q: The Model Prisons and Correctional Services Act, 2023, which was amended in the context of caste-based discrimination in prisons, is best described as
o: a guiding law prepared by the Ministry of Home Affairs for adoption by States, since prisons are a State subject
a law enacted by Parliament under Article 252 at the request of two or more States
a law enacted by Parliament under Article 253 to implement the Nelson Mandela Rules
a set of binding rules framed by the Supreme Court under Article 142
questions.e: The 2023 text is a model law. The Home Ministry drafted it to replace the colonial Prisons Act of 1894 in spirit, but each State must adopt it through its own legislature because prisons fall in the State List. The same is true of the Model Prison Manual, 2016. Both were amended after the Supreme Court condemned caste-based allocation of work and segregation in jails. Parliament has not legislated on prisons under Article 252 or Article 253.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the findings of the Panchayat Advancement Index 2.0:
1. A majority of Gram Panchayats were placed in the top two grades.
2. Participation by Gram Panchayats was higher than in the first round of the Index.
3. Uttar Pradesh had the highest proportion of its Gram Panchayats in the 'Front Runner' grade.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct: participation rose to nearly all Gram Panchayats, from about four-fifths in the first round. The results were modest. No Panchayat reached the top 'Achiever' grade and under two per cent were Front Runners; more than nine in ten were in the middle grades of Performer and Aspirant. Tripura led in the share of Front Runners, while Uttar Pradesh had only a few dozen among its many thousand Panchayats.
